request.project_description: I want to build a color-changing LED with an Arduino Uno R3. I am new to electronics and want to plan before I start.

needs_confirmation_response.project_summary: The requested color-changing effect is outside the verified first-version parts. CircuitGuard can plan a simpler project using one red LED, but it cannot plan an LED that changes color in v1.

included: A possible simpler project with one red LED, one series current-limiting resistor, a positive DC source, and ground, if the user accepts that change.
not_included: RGB, WS2812/NeoPixel, or other multi-color/addressable LEDs

questions.question: Would you like to continue with a simpler project that uses one red LED and does not change color?
questions.why_it_matters: The verified v1 reference supports one red LED only. It does not support multi-color LEDs or Arduino pin and firmware planning.

assumptions: The Arduino Uno R3 is the board the user wants to use; its electrical limits have not been verified for this plan.
safety_and_common_problems: Do not remove the series current-limiting resistor from the supported single-LED circuit.
The physical LED and resistor ratings must be confirmed before building; a simulated result does not certify the physical circuit.

can_verify: After the user accepts the supported project and its modeled circuit is configured, PhysBox can report simulated current through that red LED circuit.
cannot_verify: The color-changing effect, since multi-color LEDs are unsupported.
Arduino Uno R3 pin behavior, a physical build, or whether the board supply can provide the planned current.

limitations: This response is incomplete until the user confirms whether a single red LED project is acceptable.
No prices, part numbers, exact pin assignments, wiring diagrams, or Arduino sketch are provided.
